## Purpose

This document demonstrates reproducible R code, explanatory text and a plot.
It uses the built-in `airquality` dataset so it can run without external files.
The Practical 3 example below uses the WorldClim 2.1 January mean temperature raster.

## Inspect the data

```{r inspect}
head(airquality)
summary(airquality$Temp)
```

## Draw a plot

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, echo=FALSE}
plot(airquality$Temp, airquality$Ozone,
     xlab = "Temperature (degrees Fahrenheit)",
     ylab = "Ozone (ppb)", pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     main = "New York air quality, May–September 1973")
```

This chunk displays the plot while hiding its code with `echo=FALSE`.
Missing observations are omitted from the plot. This is an association,
not evidence of a causal effect.

## WorldClim January mean temperature

The raster is WorldClim 2.1 monthly mean temperature for January,
representing the 1970–2000 climate baseline, at 5 arc-minute resolution.
Values are in degrees Celsius. Source: [WorldClim](https://www.worldclim.org/data/worldclim21.html).
Run `source("prepare-data.R")` once if the data are missing.

```{r course-raster, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
library(terra)
library(here)
jan <- terra::rast(here("prac3_data", "wc2.1_5m_tavg_01.tif"))
plot(jan)
```

## Show code without running it

The following chunk displays code without executing it.

```{r unevaluated-example, eval=FALSE}
summary(jan)
```

## Reproducibility

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
